title: how are yall animating your AI made models?
author: Disastrous-Agency675
selftext: TBH im hoping for a method that dosnt involve retopology or having to manually re-texture the model. currently, atleast for blender, im unable to parent the rig to the model because of overlapping parts.

comments.author: reality_comes
comments.body: Codex > Astra > "rig and animate this model"

replies.author: Disastrous-Agency675
replies.body: any other ways that wont cost me a small fortune? like until the model gets bottlenecked like the rest animating a model usual costs my 2 resets

replies.author: reality_comes
replies.body: There are some local models you might be able to use to cut the cost depending on your setup. Or you could use another service that will do it

replies.author: ButterDoe
replies.body: learning to do it yourself is free

replies.author: Dangerous_Three_8506
replies.body:
Hugging Face.

Check it out!!! There is bound to be rigging there. There is also local "Codex" agents that you can learn about. Ask ChatGPT how to set everything up.

Spaces are great.

If you are serious about game development and AI then learn Hugging Face.

comments.author: josh_the_dev
comments.body: For rigging characters I use AccuRig it's free to use and the results are pretty good. For animation I mostly use ready made animations from libraries or use a video to mocap AI. Totally depends on the style your going for though

comments.author: shady101852
comments.body:
You can try [https://www.mixamo.com](https://www.mixamo.com)

Also, how did you make the model? I have trouble with that. 3D model generators come with too many issues, and any attempts i had of having Astra do it from scratch in blender ended in failure.
